newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia to grant cattle breeders 481 mln kuna in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Croatia to grant cattle breeders 481 mln kuna in 1997.

text.p: Croatia will this year grant 481 million kuna in loans to cattle breeders to boost its meat production, a government minister said on Monday.
"We shall start soon with a test loan for 3,200 heifers by granting 2,500 kuna to farmers for each heifer," Agriculture Minister Zlatko Dominikovic told a news conference.
Overall, the government plans to back up raising a total of 25,000 heifers throughout the year, but it will also cover the costs of pigs, sheep and goats, Dominikovic said.
Funds will come from foreign loans, Croatian Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the government's Agricultural Development Fund.
Individual loans will be granted at slightly under nine percent a year for four years with a grace period of one to two years, Dominikovic said.
To ease access by farmers to these funds, the loans will be handled by state-owned Postal Bank (HPB).

"The aim is to provide farmers with money ahead of spring sowing and to avoid situations when they are forced to sell too young cattle for slaughter," Dominikovic said. --Zoran Radosavljevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
